claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution for Pulumi packages.
Components inside a Pulumi package inherit the package's version.
Pulumi packages come in two flavors, and each flavor is versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository.
A source-based Pulumi package's version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow.
Publishing a source-based package to the Private Registry is typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
A semver Git tag such as `v1.2.3` is applied to the repository as the first step of publishing a source-based package.
The `pulumi package publish` CLI command sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
The `pulumi package publish` step often runs automated tests before publishing.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing a source-based package to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.
An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary.
Executable-based packages are typically distributed alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds such as npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents.
An executable-based Pulumi package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Releases of executable-based packages are produced by a CI/CD pipeline that builds the plugin, generates the SDKs, and pushes everything to the relevant feeds.
In both the source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
Pulumi recommends that a repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
A repository containing multiple Pulumi packages either has to release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights how Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
A 1:1 repository-to-package mapping keeps git tags, release artifacts, and version history aligned.
Multiple components inside a single Pulumi package are fine and expected, and they ship together at the package's version.

Pulumi recommends defining exactly one package per repository, grouping a cohesive set of components together inside that package, and using multiple repositories (one per package) to manage the distinct packages an organization publishes.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with the supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
One `PulumiPlugin.yaml` file at the repository root defines a Pulumi package.
It is technically possible to use a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components.
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components.
Bundling many unrelated components into a single package forfeits meaningful semantic versioning, which is how consumers know whether a given change is a bug fix, a new feature, or a breaking change.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way, regardless of whether each component changed.
This behavior (uniform versioning of unrelated components) violates semver, because consumers can no longer use the package version to tell whether a component they care about has actually changed.
In the example sequence, the package is released at v1.0.0 with both ComponentA and ComponentB at v1.0.0.
In the example sequence, an enhancement to ComponentA causes the package to be released at v1.1.0, even though ComponentB is unchanged.
In the example sequence, a breaking change to ComponentB causes the package to be released at v2.0.0, even though ComponentA had no change.
